review_notes: I read the whole file. The only new definition is `NumberField.ramifiedPrimes`. It is a set of natural primes `p` such that `Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn (𝓞 K) (Ideal.span {(p : ℤ)})` fails. I searched Mathlib for `ramifiedPrimes`, `ramifiedPrime` and `RamifiedPrimes`, for other ramified or unramified definitions, and for a set of ramified natural primes or ideals. I found nothing. Mathlib has only `Algebra.IsUnramifiedIn`, the infinite-place `IsUnramified` and `ramifiedPlacesOver`, and `unramifiedLocus`. None of these is a set of ramified rational primes. This definition is therefore a thin wrapper over the existing Mathlib predicate, not a competing concept. I did not check the other lemmas for duplication, since the rubric excludes standalone theorem duplication.
